article.title: Ansar Allah advances towards Saudi stronghold Aden
article.author: Aseel Saleh
article.content: As the renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Ansar Allah-led Yemeni Armed Forces enters its fourth month, developments on the ground indicate that the conflict has reached a critical threshold. However, what Riyadh and its allies could not achieve over the past decade in Yemen seems far from attainable at this point, as Ansar Allah continues to expand its territorial control and target vital Saudi sites. The last week saw a remarkable advance by Ansar Allah towards Aden, the seat of the Yemeni interim government, backed by Saudi Arabia and Western countries. Ansar Allah solidified its hold on the Khor Omairh coastline, west of Aden, and captured parts of Lahij Governorate, encompassing the highland district of Al-Maqatirah. This progress came days after the movement managed to push back Saudi-backed forces from positions overlooking the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait. The consecutive military setbacks in Yemen forced the Mohammad Bin Salman administration to sack the commander of the Saudi coalition’s joint forces, Lieutenant General Fahd al-Salman, and replace him with Saudi Arabia’s chief of general staff, General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili. Overwhelmed by Ansar Allah’s territorial gains during ground clashes, Saudi Arabia intensified its airstrikes across Yemen, with the latest strike on Friday, November 20, targeting Hodeidah port , a major Red Sea maritime harbor. The port was struck despite previous port-for-port retaliation threats by Ansar Allah, after Saudi Arabia had warned of launching the assault hours earlier. The Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson, Brigadier General Yahya Saree, issued a series of statements vowing that Ansar Allah would target all Saudi ports on the Red Sea should Hodeidah be attacked. “The Armed Forces announce that Jeddah Port and all Saudi enemy ports on the Red Sea coast will be targets for our forces if the enemy carries out its threats to bombard Hodeidah Port,” Saree said. He further cautioned “employees, workers and those present near them to evacuate immediately and stay away.” All shipping companies were also urged “to evacuate their vessels from those ports immediately.” Moreover, the Yemeni Ministry of Electricity and Energy reported on Friday that Saudi warplanes targeted power generation stations in Mocha, Taiz, and in Saadah. In response, Ansar Allah attacked Saudi Arabia’s Al-Shuqaiq power plant and the port of Jazan.
